edges.reason: Constructor assigns msg.sender to the owner state variable, creating a single privileged account
owner is written from the untrusted constructor caller without any validation
latestDifficultyPeriodStarted is initialised from the block number at deployment time
Constructor invokes _startNewMiningEpoch to create the first mining challenge
mint uses msg.sender inside the proof of work digest and credits the reward to the caller
Nonce parameter feeds the keccak256 digest used to validate the solution
Caller supplied challenge_digest is compared with the locally computed digest
The mining challenge is derived from a previous Ethereum block hash, a block context dependency
mint reads the caller balance before adding the mined reward
mint computes digest = keccak256(challengeNumber, msg.sender, nonce)
mint caches solutionForChallenge[challengeNumber] into the solution local before overwriting
reward_amount is computed from the halving arithmetic in getMiningReward
Mined reward is credited to the balances mapping of msg.sender
tokensMinted accumulates each reward, later guarded by assert against maxSupplyForEra
mint asserts tokensMinted <= maxSupplyForEra, an assertion failure burns all gas
lastRewardTo diagnostic field is set to the untrusted msg.sender
lastRewardAmount diagnostic field is set from the computed reward
A successful mint triggers _startNewMiningEpoch to generate the next challenge
mint calls getMiningReward to determine the payout size
Epoch rollover compares tokensMinted plus the next reward against maxSupplyForEra
maxSupplyForEra is recomputed with the expression _totalSupply - _totalSupply / (2**(rewardEra+1))
Era supply and reward arithmetic rely on 2**exponent operations with shifting bases
rewardEra is incremented up to the hard cap of 19, halving the reward each era
epochCount is incremented on every epoch rollover
Difficulty readjustment is invoked whenever epochCount divides evenly by _BLOCKS_PER_READJUSTMENT
challengeNumber is assigned block.blockhash(block.number - 1), a block context dependency
Difficulty retargeting reads the block-number based latestDifficultyPeriodStarted
ethBlocksSinceLastDifficultyPeriod = block.number - latestDifficultyPeriodStarted
The elapsed block count is used as a divisor, which can be zero in the same block as the period start
Difficulty adjustment performs unchecked multiplications, divisions and subtractions on the target
excess_block_pct derives from division of percentages and can underflow on subtraction of 100
excess_block_pct_extra clamps the percentage with limitLessThan after a subtraction that can underflow
miningTarget is increased or decreased based on the computed percentages
Current miningTarget is read to compute the next difficulty value
latestDifficultyPeriodStarted is reset to block.number after each retarget
Mining reward is halved according to the current rewardEra index
Reward computation performs 25000000000 / (2**rewardEra), vulnerable to exponent shifting
getMiningDifficulty reads the _MAXIMUM_TARGET constant as the numerator
getMiningDifficulty divides _MAXIMUM_TARGET by miningTarget, which can be zeroed by retargeting
getMiningTarget exposes the mutable miningTarget state variable
getChallengeNumber exposes a value derived from an Ethereum block hash
totalSupply returns _totalSupply minus the zero address balance
totalSupply reads the balances mapping for the zero address
balanceOf reads the balances mapping for the supplied owner
transfer credits tokens to the recipient parameter
transfer debits the caller balance by the tokens parameter
transfer debits balances of the untrusted msg.sender
transfer writes updated balances for sender and recipient
approve writes the allowance keyed by the untrusted msg.sender
approve stores the spender allowance in the allowed mapping
transferFrom debits the from account balance parameter
transferFrom credits the to account balance parameter
transferFrom debits both balance and allowance by the tokens parameter
transferFrom consumes the allowance granted to the untrusted msg.sender
transferFrom writes updated balances for the from and to accounts
transferFrom writes the reduced spender allowance in the allowed mapping
allowance reads the allowed mapping for the owner and spender pair
approveAndCall stores the allowance keyed by the untrusted msg.sender
The attacker controlled spender parameter is later invoked as an external contract
approveAndCall stores the tokens parameter as the allowance value
Opaque attacker supplied data is forwarded into the external callback call
approveAndCall writes the new allowance before making the external call
approveAndCall invokes receiveApproval on the untrusted spender contract, enabling reentrancy
The external spender contract regains execution control inside approveAndCall before it returns
Fallback function is reached by any untrusted caller sending ether and always reverts
transferAnyERC20Token requires msg.sender to equal the stored owner address
Owner privilege check compares the untrusted caller with the owner state variable
Arbitrary tokenAddress parameter is cast to ERC20Interface and called externally
tokens parameter specifies the amount forwarded to the external token transfer
transferAnyERC20Token makes an external call to a caller supplied token contract
The untrusted token contract executes its own code and can reenter before returning
getMintDigest mixes the untrusted msg.sender into the debug digest
Nonce parameter is hashed together with the challenge and sender address
The supplied challenge_number parameter is recomputed into a digest for off-chain comparison
checkMintSolution hashes the supplied nonce into the digest
Supplied challenge_digest is compared against the recomputed digest
Caller supplied testTarget is used in a raw comparison against uint256(digest)
checkMintSolution includes the untrusted msg.sender in the recomputed digest

normalization_plan.reason: The nonce parameter exists only to build the keccak256 digest validated inside mint and carries no independent identity
The caller supplied digest is immediately compared with the mint computed digest and then discarded
Local digest is a transient keccak256 result used solely for the comparison and storage inside mint
Local solution only caches solutionForChallenge[challengeNumber] to detect a repeated reward inside mint
Reward local flows directly into balances, tokensMinted and the diagnostics fields of mint
The recipient parameter is used only to index the balances mapping written by transfer
The amount parameter is consumed only by the SafeMath add and sub calls inside transfer
The from parameter only indexes the balance and allowance mappings modified by transferFrom
The to parameter only indexes the recipient balance entry updated by transferFrom
The amount parameter is consumed only by the SafeMath calls inside transferFrom
The spender parameter is the untrusted target of the external receiveApproval call and should be tied to that unsafe operation
The tokens parameter only sets the allowed mapping entry written by approveAndCall
The opaque data parameter is forwarded verbatim into the external callback call
The tokenAddress parameter is cast to ERC20Interface and becomes the target of the external call
The tokens parameter only parameterises the amount forwarded in the owner sweep
This local is the divisor of the retarget percentage formula and can be zero, so it maps to that arithmetic operation
The percentage local is produced directly by the unchecked division inside _reAdjustDifficulty
The clamped percentage local exists only to scale miningTarget inside the difficulty retarget function
The nonce parameter is only hashed to build the debug digest returned by checkMintSolution
The expected digest parameter is only used in the equality comparison performed by checkMintSolution
The caller supplied target parameter only feeds the uint256(digest) comparison in checkMintSolution
The nonce parameter is only concatenated into the keccak256 computation of getMintDigest
The challenge parameter only supplies the first input of the debug digest computation
